title: Declarative Table Partitioning
description: Partition massive tables by RANGE, LIST, and HASH, understand partition pruning, and maintain zero-latency queries.

data.text: When a table grows past tens of millions of rows, B-tree indexes no longer fit in memory (`shared_buffers`), leading to severe cache miss penalties. **Declarative Partitioning** splits a single logical table into smaller physical tables (partitions) based on a partition key.

When a query filters by the partition key (`WHERE created_at >= '2024-01-01'`), the query planner performs **Partition Pruning**, skipping completely irrelevant partitions and scanning only the target partition.

data.title: Declarative Range Partitioning by Year
data.content: Creating a partitioned parent table and bound child partitions.

data.text: A partitioned table only stores data in partitions that exist, so an insert with a partition key outside every bound fails until you create the matching partition. In practice you create future partitions ahead of time — with a scheduled job or a tool like `pg_partman` — so writes never hit a missing range. Old partitions are expired by dropping them, which is a metadata operation rather than a large `DELETE`.

data.title: Attach a future partition and drop an expired one
data.content: Creating partitions for future months ahead of time keeps inserts from failing. Detaching and dropping a whole partition is instant compared to deleting its rows.

data.title: Pruning needs the partition key in the predicate
data.text: If the query does not filter on the partition key, the planner must scan every partition, so a partitioned table can be slower than a single table because of the extra planning and per-partition overhead. Filter or join on the partition column directly, avoid wrapping it in a function, and remember that a partition index is a local index: it does not speed a query that spans every partition.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Declarative partitioning splits tables by `RANGE`, `LIST`, or `HASH`.
Partition pruning skips scanning unneeded child partitions.
Dropping an old partition (`DROP TABLE audit_logs_2020`) takes milliseconds and reclaims disk space instantly without VACUUM overhead.
